youtube.baslik: Epley or Semont: which maneuver works better? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: For posterior canal BPPV, the Epley and Semont maneuvers are used, and comparative studies have generally found similar effectiveness. Epley uses slower transitions but requires extending the head backward; Semont needs no neck extension but requires a fast, wide body movement. The maneuver is done by a qualified, trained clinician who has confirmed the diagnosis with positional testing, in a suitable patient; this video is not a self-treatment guide.

Two maneuvers are common for posterior canal BPPV: Epley and Semont.
Epley uses slower transitions, but requires extending the head backward.
Semont needs no neck extension, but requires a fast body movement.
Comparative studies have generally found their effectiveness similar.
A trained clinician who confirmed the diagnosis chooses for each patient.
